q: A rule of thumb used for estimating materials on a residential project:
n: A common rule of thumb for residential projects puts materials at about 70% of construction cost and labour at 30%. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate; Philippine estimating practice.

q: Awell-managed office is like a car that:
o: Has plenty of gas and oil
n: A well-managed office, like a well-tuned car, runs smoothly, with systems and people working together without friction. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 200 series (office management).

q: As a veteran architect with your own architectural practice, why do you need a secretary?
o: To prepare contract documents and keep track of various on-going projects
n: A practice's secretary keeps office records, files and correspondence in order. Contract documents remain the architect's work. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (AIA).

q: You paid ₱1,000,000, VAT inclusive, for office furniture. How much was VAT?
n: VAT inside a VAT-inclusive price is 12/112 of the price: ₱1,000,000 × 12/112 = ₱107,142.86. Source: NIRC, Sec. 106.

q: After passing the architecture licensure examination, you and your classmates have managed to set up an architecture practice in your hometown. What is the first thing to do?
o: Go SEC and register your company
Go DTl and get a business name
n: A new practice starts by setting its goals and objectives (a business plan), before registering and hiring. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (AIA).

q: Asa practicing architect, what would you think is the purpose of hiring an accountant?
n: An accountant keeps the practice's books, taxes and finances in order, for financial stability. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (AIA).

q: A Filipino architect with long overseas experience is asked to design a house in Malaysia. How can he practice there legally?
n: Under the ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services, a registered ASEAN Architect may practise in another ASEAN country in collaboration with a local architect. Source: ASEAN Mutual Recognition Arrangement on Architectural Services (2007).

q: What does reciprocity mean in the cross-border practice of architecture?
o: Set up an office overseas with reciprocity
Get projects without a licensure exam
Practice and collaborate with local architects
n: Reciprocity in cross-border practice means a foreign architect may practise in a host country in collaboration with local architects, on terms equal to that country's own professionals. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27 and 38; ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services.

q: What would you wear if you are going to work as an apprentice?
n: An apprentice spends much time drafting and on site, so relaxed, comfortable but neat work clothes suit the role. Business attire is kept for client meetings. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (AIA); UAP office practice.

q: After passing the board exam, a lot of new architects are very proud and becoming boastful. What would be the best way to start a career as a Registered and Licensed Architect?
o: Accept only a good salary because you are already RLA
Accept current salary from your mentor and gain good experience
Resign immediately from your mentor because he cannot increase your salary
n: A new RLA builds his career best by staying humble, accepting a fair salary from his mentor and gaining broad experience before going independent. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct; UAP mentoring guidance.

q: Architectural practice is one of the most stressful jobs in the world, and many are committed to project deadlines, with some working their entire lives without being appreciated. In practice, there is always a deadline. What would you do if the deadline falls on Sunday?
o: Deadline is important, you must be there on Sunday
Ask the Principal to move the deadline
Stay home; it's not a working day
n: Plan ahead: finish work before a deadline that falls on a non-working day, such as by Friday, rather than miss it or demand an extension. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (project management).

q: In practice, the most challenging part of surviving your office is financial stability, followed by your ability to get new projects from time to time. What do you think is the reason why architects should hire a secretary?
o: Asecretary helps organize the architect's documents and time
Asecretary records meetings and reminds architects
Asecretary helps architects to be inspired every morning
Architects are not good at management, and a secretary will always be by their side to manage their time
n: A secretary helps organize the architect's documents, schedule and time so he can focus on design and clients. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (office administration).

q: What is the best thing to do to get projects continuously?
o: Anarchitect should gain a good network from developers
Improve your design to international standards and properly manage clients
Geta business development executive and market your practice
n: Continuous work comes from good, competitive design and well-managed client relationships, which bring repeat clients and referrals. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (marketing and client relations).

q: What is the best thing to do to get projects internationally?
o: Geta specialization and be recognized for it internationally
Go and have a beautiful marketing agent get projects for you
Study abroad and gain a network
n: To get international projects, collaborate with international practices, which also respects host-country licensing rules. Source: ASEAN MRA on Architectural Services; RA 9266, Sec. 38.

q: After graduating from a BS Architecture program in the Philippines, an architecture graduate worked in Saudi Arabia for two years before deciding to retum to the Philippines to take the Architecture Licensure Exam. What must be done to file the requirements?
o: Have the DT form signed by another Filipino architect in the Philippines
Take the ALE in Saudi Arabia if available
Fill out the DT form and have it signed by a foreign mentor
The mentor must be a Filipino RLA, even if working abroad, to qualify
n: The LEA's diversified-experience form must be certified by a Filipino RLA as mentor, even if the work was done abroad. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 13; PRBOA resolutions on diversified experience.

q: After gaining work experience abroad, the architecture graduate plans to return to the Philippines and help establish an architectural firm with their employer. What is the first step to register the business?
o: Register with PRC, then DTI and DOLE
Register first with DTI and secure a business permit
n: A firm set up with partners or an employer as a corporation registers first with the SEC. Sole proprietors register with the DTI. Source: RA 11232 (Revised Corporation Code); RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: What form of compensation applies for preparing feasibility studies and marketing materials?
n: Feasibility studies and marketing materials are time-based, non-creative work, best paid by a multiple of direct personnel expenses. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201 and 202 (MDPE).

q: When is the architect entitled to receive payment for feasibility studies and marketing materials?
n: For a discrete package of studies and marketing materials, payment is due on submission of all deliverables, as the agreement sets. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: Acouple plans to build a convention center for at least 800 persons. They hire an architect for the project, who later recommends hiring a professional consultant in hospitality design due to limited experience in that field. Whom should they hire?
n: The right specialist for hospitality design is a hospitality architect, a consulting architect with expertise in that building type. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (consulting architect); 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 209.

q: Regarding the same convention center project, who is considered the prime professional?
o: The architect and the hospitality professional
n: The architect remains the prime professional, coordinating all consultants including the hospitality specialist. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: Who is responsible for paying the hospitality consultant in the convention center project?
o: The architect and the consultant, sharing the contract price
The project owner, paying the consultant directly
The architect, from their contract price
n: Specialist consultants the owner engages on the architect's recommendation are paid directly by the project owner, outside the architect's fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (owner's responsibilities).

q: What does an acoustician do in a convention center design?
o: Ensure sound insulation and acoustic treatment
n: An acoustician designs sound insulation and room acoustics: reverberation, noise control and speech intelligibility. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; Long, Architectural Acoustics.

q: An architect wants to be featured in a magazine for their firm's 25th anniversary. To lower the cost, with consent, a writer friend solicits advertisements under the architect's name. Is there anything wrong?
o: Nothing is wrong; all parties gave consent
n: Soliciting advertisements under the architect's name is self-promotion through paid publicity, which breaks the Code. The architect is liable even if he consented. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the public).

q: What action should an architect take if they believe their work has been misattributed or plagiarized?
o: Request a public apology from the featured architect
File a complaint with the PRC
Contact the NBI for an investigation
Send a cease-and-desist letter to the publisher
n: Misattribution or plagiarism of an architect's work violates RA 9266 and the Code of Ethical Conduct. It is filed as a complaint with the PRC Board of Architecture. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22 and 33; PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: What is the standard minimum fee for designing a private residence?
n: A private residence is Group 4, with a recommended DAEDS fee of 10% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4.

q: What is the right alternative after passing the board exam?
o: Take a secondary complementing course related to business
Work in a company to gain more experience
n: After passing the board exam, the sound path is to work in a firm to gain practical experience before practising independently. Source: UAP Continuing Professional Development guidance; RA 10912 (CPD Act).

q: As anew licensed architect starting to practice, what is the best thing to do?
o: Continue working in a firm and gain more experience
n: A newly licensed architect does best to keep working in a firm and gain more experience before practising alone. Source: UAP mentoring guidance; RA 10912 (CPD Act).

q: What would be the best dress for an Architect if he is going to meet the client?
o: Any kind of dress he/she wants
n: Business attire is appropriate when meeting a client. It presents the architect professionally. Source: Demkin, The Architect's Handbook of Professional Practice (client relations).

q: Under the Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232), what is the minimum number of incorporators?
n: The Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232, 2019) allows a one-person corporation, so the minimum number of incorporators is 1. Source: RA 11232, Sec. 10 and 115.

q: What is the minimum number of partners in a partnership?
n: A partnership needs at least two partners. Two or more persons contribute money, property or industry to a common fund to share the profits. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1767.

q: For a design-build project, who keeps the record on site?
n: In design-build the design-builder (contractor) runs the site and keeps the site records. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 207.

q: Why may an architect keep the original plans from the owner?
o: The owner is entitled only to blueprints
They are covered by intellectual property law
n: The original plans are the architect's intellectual property (instruments of service). The owner receives copies for his project. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33; RA 8293.

q: Where does an architect register a single proprietorship?
n: A single proprietorship registers its business name with the DTI. Source: Act 3883 (Business Name Law) as amended; DTI BNRS.

q: What must be secured before applying for a business permit?
n: A barangay clearance must be secured before applying for a business (mayor's) permit. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 152(c).

q: Where do you apply for a business permit?
n: Business permits are applied for at the city or municipal hall, through the Business Permits and Licensing Office. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 444/455; RA 11032 (Ease of Doing Business Act).

q: What defines a successful architect?
n: A successful architect is defined by good workmanship and ethics. Undercutting fees to win projects is unethical. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.
